subject: Kavi AI — LlamaIndex sidecar instrumentation & sandbox playbook
messages:
From: Eliot Summers <eliot.summers@kavi.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Partnerships <partners@kavi.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: LlamaIndex sidecar: lightweight tracing & instrumentation for Kavi sandbox

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Kavi is building a managed sandbox for customers to bring their own document stacks with LlamaIndex (we already have adapters + ingestion flows). We're exploring a lightweight "sidecar" approach where Redwood's SDK would run alongside the LlamaIndex runtime to capture traces, token-level latency, and a small set of application-level metrics (query id, root prompt hash, retrieval keys) without requiring customers to change their embeddings pipeline.

High-level asks from our engineering team:
- Feasibility assessment: can Redwood offer a sidecar SDK that instruments LlamaIndex processes (Python 3.10) with minimal CPU/memory overhead?
- Example integration points: tracing hooks, KV cache correlation, and optional prefix caching signals.
- Security/PII: can we avoid sending raw doc contents to Redwood hosted telemetry? We prefer hashed keys and sampled traces.
- Trial: a 2-week sandbox pilot with ~50 internal eval users to validate latency and token counts.

I've attached a short proposal and a checklist of the signals we'd like to capture. Can we set up a tech sync this week? Our lead engineer (cc'd in partners@) is available Wed-Fri in the afternoon PT.

Best,
Eliot
Director, Partnerships — Kavi AI

Attachments: kavi-sidecar-proposal-v1.pdf (application/pdf), sidecar-instrumentation-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Summers <eliot.summers@kavi.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LlamaIndex sidecar: lightweight tracing & instrumentation for Kavi sandbox

Hi Eliot — great summary, thanks.

We're very interested in this pattern; we see multiple ISVs asking for low-friction instrumentation that doesn't force full model routing changes. Quick answers up front:
- Feasibility: yes — our SDK can run as a sidecar process and provide non-blocking gRPC/HTTP stream exports for traces and token metrics. We have a small-footprint Python shim used in a few pilots that targets PY3.9/3.10.
- Integration points: we can wire tracing hooks into LlamaIndex's Retriever and Query pipeline; also expose a small KV correlation library so you can correlate retrieval keys with Redwood's cache hits.
- PII model: our default is to avoid sending raw document text. We support hashed identifiers, selective redaction, and sampling controls. Full content transfers are optional and require a different consent flow.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech sync Wed 2027-03-03 at 2:00pm PT — 30m (we'll bring Aditya from runtime+Marissa for partner ops)
2) Redwood will run an internal perf sweep on the sidecar with representative LlamaIndex workloads and share baseline numbers (CPU, memory, token overhead) before the pilot.
3) Kick off a 2-week sandbox pilot with instrumentation toggles and a short eval rubric.

If that works, I'll schedule the meeting and circulate a short playbook.

— Grace
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: internal: Kavi sidecar sync prep + perf checklist

Team — prepping for Wed's sync. Quick notes / asks so we come aligned:

1) Scope of instrumentation (we should confirm specific LlamaIndex hooks):
   - Retriever.get_relevant_documents
   - QueryEngine.run (including prompt template id + prompt hash)
   - Embedding calls (hash + token counts, not raw vectors)

2) Performance targets to validate in our perf sweep:
   - Added p95 latency per call: <10ms
   - CPU overhead: <5% on a 4-core dev node when under synthetic load
   - Memory: sidecar <150MB resident

3) Telemetry controls: sampling rate, PII redaction toggle, and on-device aggregation window (default 2s).

4) Security: confirm TLS mutual auth option for sidecar -> Redwood endpoint, and a default hashed-id-only flow for PII-sensitive customers.

5) Deliverables before pilot start (Mar 8):
   - perf_report.csv (baseline vs instrumented)
   - sidecar-build artifact (wheel + small docker image)
   - short playbook: how to enable/disable instrumentation per workspace

Connor — can you help own the perf sweep and the checklist spreadsheet? Marissa — I'll rely on you for pilot success criteria and partner ops runbook. Grace — please confirm Wed time and I'll draft the perf plan.

Thanks,
Aditya
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Eliot Summers <eliot.summers@kavi.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kavi AI — LlamaIndex sidecar instrumentation & sandbox playbook

Thanks all — Wed 2pm PT is perfect. Our engineering lead (Hannah Li) will join from Kavi and can share some small-scale query traces to make the perf sweep realistic.

A couple clarifications from our side before the sync:
- We prefer hashed doc ids + retrieval keys only; no raw text for the pilot.
- For quota billing, we'd like to understand token accounting: will instrumented counters be counted toward Redwood hosted usage or purely telemetry (no billable token charges)?

We're excited to run the sandbox — if the perf looks good we'll look to expand to a small co-sell lab for select prospects.

Best,
Eliot
Director, Partnerships — Kavi AI
